chapter: Building the band, Ivie Anderson and touring
title: Harry Carney joins at Salem Willows
summary: Carney was hired as a kid for the summer in New England and only became a full member at the Cotton Club.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Now, Harry Carney came in the band before you all went to the Cotton Club.
As you got ready to go?

No. Harry Carney never become a full-fledged member of our band until we went to the Cotton Club, he never. Carney and Johnny Hodges, they never -- we enlarged the band. Carney used to play with us when we went up for the summer in Salem, Willows, he played with us. We gave him a job, he was justa little kid. We just gave him a job, but when we went to the Kentucky Club, of course, we went up to New England for Sy Clarit Schribman and that's when Carney joined us up there.
What kind of a gig was that, in Salem?
That was a whole summer, a summer gig. From Decoration Day to Labor Day, all summer.
Now,did you play a different program of music at the Salem Willows than you did at the Kentucky Club?

No, we played the same style we played when we had the Kentucky -- had the Washingtonians and because it was different -- the sound was different. We kept that sound always, but we didn't play no different style.
